```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sabo_2026_hydroxyurea"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sabo_2026_hydroxyurea"))$description`
* Article: [Pharmaceutics 18(6):654 (2026)](https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18060654)
* Supplement: <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/pharmaceutics18060654/s1>

# Population

The model was fitted to the OPTIMDREP randomised trial (NCT06464458) in
Strasbourg, France: 22 patients with sickle cell disease (14 male, 8 female)
taking once-daily oral hydroxyurea, of whom 20 were children (median age 9.7
years, range 2.5-16.4; median weight 31.0 kg, range 11.4-60.0 kg) and 2 were
adult women (29.1 and 35.7 years). Across the whole cohort the mean age was
12.2 +/- 7.7 years and the mean weight 35.8 +/- 16.7 kg. The daily dose was
20.3 +/- 2.4 mg/kg; 17 of 22 patients were already at steady state and 5 were
starting treatment. Renal function was normal (cystatin C-based eGFR 126.7
+/- 14.2 mL/min/1.73 m2). Sources: Sabo 2026 Table 1 and Results 3.1.

Full pharmacokinetic profiles (pre-dose, 10 and 20 min, 1, 2, 4 and 6 h) were
taken at the first visit (V0) and the fifth (V5), and a two-hour concentration
at visits V1-V4: 391 concentrations in all. Non-compartmental analysis split the
44 full profiles into two absorption phenotypes by their observed Tmax: rapid
(Tmax < 1 h, 16 profiles, 36.4%) and slow (Tmax >= 1 h). The phenotype is the
model's covariate on the absorption rate constant.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Sabo_2026_hydroxyurea")()$population`).

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Sabo_2026_hydroxyurea.R`. The table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka, slow absorber) | log(1.36) 1/h | Table 2, ka row (RSE 14.80%) |
| `lcl` (CL/F at 34.9 kg) | log(9.06) L/h | Table 2, Cl/F row (RSE 4.71%) |
| `lvc` (V/F at 34.9 kg) | log(25.23) L | Table 2, Vd/F row (RSE 7.69%) |
| `e_abs_rapid_ka` | 1.99 | Table 2, beta_ka_KINETIC row (RSE 21.20%); Results 3.2.2 (ka 9.93 vs 1.36 1/h) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.64 | Table 2, beta_Cl_NBW row (RSE 13.90%) |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.80 | Table 2, beta_Vd_NBW row (RSE 14.80%) |
| `etalka` | log(1 + 0.6407^2) | Table 2 IIV-ka 64.07%; Supplementary Table S3 'IIV final model (CV%)' |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.3299^2) | Table 2 IIV-Cl/F 32.99%; Supplementary Table S3 |
| `etalvc` | log(1 + 0.3473^2) | Table 2 IIV-Vd/F 34.73%; Supplementary Table S3 |
| `addSd` | 1.60 mg/L | Table 2 residual error a (RSE 8.88%) |
| `propSd` | 0.35 | Table 2 residual error b (RSE 6.33%) |
| `ka <- exp(lka + e_abs_rapid_ka * ABS_RAPID + etalka)` | n/a | Eq. 2 |
| `vc <- exp(lvc + etalvc) * (WT / 34.9)^e_wt_vc` | n/a | Eq. 3; Table 4 (34.9 kg = median weight) |
| `cl <- exp(lcl + etalcl) * (WT / 34.9)^e_wt_cl` | n/a | Eq. 4 |
| One compartment, first-order absorption, linear elimination | n/a | Results 3.2.2; Supplementary Table S2 'Final model' |
| `Cc ~ add(addSd) + prop(propSd) + combined1()` | n/a | Results 3.2.2 ('combined additive ... and proportional') |

# Typical-value checks

The rapid-absorber ka follows from Eq. 2, and with linear elimination the
exposure after a single dose is `dose / CL`. Both are checked against a
typical-value solve.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Sabo_2026_hydroxyurea")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Eq. 2: ka for a rapid absorber = 1.36 * exp(1.99); the paper reports 9.93 1/h.
ka_rapid <- 1.36 * exp(1.99)
stopifnot(abs(ka_rapid / 9.93 - 1) < 0.005)

wt_ref <- 34.9
dose_ref <- 20.3 * wt_ref
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_ref, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 48, by = 0.05), cmt = "central")
typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ,
    params = c(WT = wt_ref, ABS_RAPID = 1), rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
  )) |> dplyr::mutate(phenotype = "rapid"),
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ,
    params = c(WT = wt_ref, ABS_RAPID = 0), rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
  )) |> dplyr::mutate(phenotype = "slow")
)

typ_summary <- typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(phenotype) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    ka = ka[1],
    Cmax = max(Cc),
    Tmax = time[which.max(Cc)],
    AUC0_48 = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(AUC_closed_form = dose_ref / 9.06)
knitr::kable(typ_summary, digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical 34.9-kg patient after a single 20.3 mg/kg dose.")

# Linear elimination: AUC is dose / CL whatever the absorption phenotype. The
# trapezoid on a 0.05-h grid to 48 h (about 25 half-lives) is within 0.1%.
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_summary$AUC0_48 / typ_summary$AUC_closed_form - 1) < 0.002))
stopifnot(abs(typ_summary$ka[typ_summary$phenotype == "rapid"] - ka_rapid) < 1e-8)
```

The half-life of a typical patient is `log(2) * 25.23 / 9.06` =
`r round(log(2) * 25.23 / 9.06, 2)` h, so once-daily dosing leaves
`r signif(100 * exp(-24 * 9.06 / 25.23), 2)`% of a dose at the next one.
Steady state and a first dose therefore give the same profile, and the
simulations below use a single dose.

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. Weights are log-normal with the Table 1
mean and SD (35.8 +/- 16.7 kg), truncated to 11.4-70 kg, and doses are drawn
around the Table 1 mean of 20.3 +/- 2.4 mg/kg. Three cohorts of 200 are
simulated: all rapid absorbers, all slow absorbers, and a mixed cohort in which
each patient is rapid with probability 0.364, the fraction of rapid profiles in
the study.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(654)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(654)

# The paper's full-profile sampling times plus a denser grid for the figures.
t_paper <- c(0, 1 / 6, 1 / 3, 1, 2, 4, 6)
t_obs <- sort(unique(c(t_paper, seq(0, 8, by = 0.1))))

make_cohort <- function(n, phenotype, p_rapid, id_offset) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (16.7 / 35.8)^2))
  wt <- exp(rnorm(n, log(35.8) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog))
  wt <- pmin(pmax(wt, 11.4), 70)
  subj <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = wt,
    ABS_RAPID = rbinom(n, 1, p_rapid),
    dose = round(rnorm(n, 20.3, 2.4) * wt),
    phenotype = phenotype
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    subj |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot"),
    subj |>
      tidyr::crossing(time = t_obs) |>
      dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort(200, "rapid", 1, 0L),
  make_cohort(200, "slow", 0, 200L),
  make_cohort(200, "mixed", 0.364, 400L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events,
  keep = c("phenotype", "ABS_RAPID", "WT", "dose")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-1b}
# Replicates Figure 1b of Sabo 2026: mean concentration-time profile by
# absorption phenotype over the 0-6 h sampling window.
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(phenotype != "mixed", time <= 6) |>
  dplyr::group_by(phenotype, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_Cc = mean(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, mean_Cc, colour = phenotype)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Mean hydroxyurea concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "Absorption phenotype",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1b of Sabo 2026 (individual predictions).")
```

```{r figure-4}
# Replicates Figure 4b-c of Sabo 2026: VPC by absorption phenotype (simulated
# observations including residual error; 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles).
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(phenotype != "mixed", time <= 6) |>
  dplyr::group_by(phenotype, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~phenotype) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Hydroxyurea concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4b-c of Sabo 2026 (KINETIC = 0 slow, 1 rapid).")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper's non-compartmental analysis used the observed concentrations at the
seven sampling times, AUC0-6h by the trapezoidal rule, and AUCinf = AUC0-6h +
C6h / lambda_z with lambda_z from the last two points (Methods 2.4.1). The same
calculation is repeated here at the same times, on two versions of the
simulated data: the individual predictions (`Cc`), and simulated observations
including residual error (`sim`), from which values below the 0.79 mg/L lower
limit of quantification are removed. The second is the like-for-like
comparison with observed data for Cmax and Tmax, because the maximum of seven
noisy samples sits above the maximum of the noise-free curve. AUCinf and CL/F
are computed on the individual predictions only: with a 35% proportional error
the two-point lambda_z of a simulated profile is often near zero or negative,
and the extrapolated area is then unbounded.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% t_paper, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, phenotype, Cc, sim) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, sim), names_to = "prediction", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    prediction = dplyr::recode(prediction,
      Cc = "individual prediction",
      sim = "with residual error"
    ),
    # Pre-dose concentration is zero for both versions; elsewhere drop simulated
    # observations below the assay LLOQ.
    conc = dplyr::if_else(time == 0, 0, conc)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0 | prediction == "individual prediction" | conc >= 0.79) |>
  dplyr::mutate(hl_points = time %in% c(4, 6))

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, phenotype) |>
  tidyr::crossing(prediction = c("individual prediction", "with residual error"))
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | phenotype + prediction + id)

# Cmax, Tmax and AUC0-6h for every profile.
nca_main <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, conc ~ time | phenotype + prediction + id),
  dose_obj,
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = c(6, Inf),
    auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE), tmax = c(FALSE, TRUE)
  )
))

# AUCinf and CL/F use the paper's two-point lambda_z from the 4-h and 6-h
# samples, on the individual predictions only. With a 35% proportional error
# the two-point slope of simulated observations is often near zero or
# negative, and the resulting AUCinf values are unbounded.
ipred_only <- function(x) dplyr::filter(x, prediction == "individual prediction")
# A two-point fit has no adjusted r-squared; PKNCA warns once per such fit.
# That warning is expected here and is the only one muffled.
nca_tail <- withCallingHandlers(
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(ipred_only(nca_input),
      conc ~ time | phenotype + prediction + id,
      include_half.life = "hl_points"
    ),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ipred_only(dose_df), amt ~ time | phenotype + prediction + id),
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
  )),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("adj.r.squared", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
)

nca_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(as.data.frame(nca_main), as.data.frame(nca_tail))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

The paper reports arithmetic means (Results 3.2.1), so the simulated values are
summarised as means too.

```{r nca-compare}
sim_means <- nca_long |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "cl.obs")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(phenotype, prediction, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# The paper's overall means come from all 44 profiles, a mix of rapid and slow;
# they are compared with the mixed cohort.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~phenotype, ~prediction, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~cl.obs,
  "mixed", "individual prediction", 27.5, 1.07, 72.9, 101.2, 9.1,
  "mixed", "with residual error", 27.5, 1.07, 72.9, NA, NA,
  "rapid", "individual prediction", 36.5, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "rapid", "with residual error", 36.5, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "slow", "individual prediction", 22.3, NA, NA, NA, NA,
  "slow", "with residual error", 22.3, NA, NA, NA, NA
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_means,
  reference = published,
  by = c("phenotype", "prediction"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "mg*h/L",
    aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", cl.obs = "L/h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  # Keep only rows with a published value (the others carry a dash).
  dplyr::filter(grepl("[0-9]", Reference))

knitr::kable(cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated vs. published mean NCA (Sabo 2026 Results 3.2.1).",
    "AUC0-6h is reported as AUClast over 0-6 h.",
    "* differs from reference by >20%."
  )
)
```

```{r nca-gate}
get_mean <- function(pheno, pred, code) {
  v <- sim_means$PPORRES[sim_means$phenotype == pheno &
    sim_means$prediction == pred & sim_means$PPTESTCD == code]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique simulated mean for ", pheno, "/", pred, "/", code)
  v
}
ipred <- "individual prediction"
obs <- "with residual error"
# Exposure and clearance carry the structural parameters (CL/F, its weight
# exponent, the dose), so a mis-transcription moves them by tens of percent.
# The mean of 200 subjects with 33% CV on CL/F has a standard error near 3%.
# Realised about -18% (AUCinf), -14% (AUC0-6h) and +5% (CL/F); the AUC
# shortfall is discussed below, and 30% still fails on a doubled or halved
# clearance, volume or dose.
stopifnot(
  abs(get_mean("mixed", ipred, "aucinf.obs") / 101.2 - 1) < 0.30,
  abs(get_mean("mixed", ipred, "cl.obs") / 9.1 - 1) < 0.30,
  abs(get_mean("mixed", ipred, "auclast") / 72.9 - 1) < 0.30
)
# The phenotype acts on Cmax: the paper's rapid/slow ratio of means is
# 36.5 / 22.3 = 1.64. An effect lost or inverted (e_abs_rapid_ka = 0 or
# negative) gives a ratio at or below 1.
cmax_ratio <- get_mean("rapid", obs, "cmax") / get_mean("slow", obs, "cmax")
stopifnot(cmax_ratio > 1.3, cmax_ratio < 2.2)
```

The simulated mean CL/F agrees with the observed mean (about +5%), and the
rapid/slow Cmax ratio (about 1.6) matches the observed 36.5 / 22.3 = 1.64.
Exposure is lower than observed: AUC0-6h by about 14% and AUCinf by about 18%.
The simulated Cmax is lower in both phenotypes, by about 30% for the
individual predictions and about 13% once residual error is added and the
maximum is read from the seven sampled concentrations, as for the observed
data. The flagged Tmax with residual error reflects noisy samples near the
peak moving the observed maximum to a later sampling time.

Two features of the study, rather than of the parameters, are the likely
reasons for the lower exposure. First, the observed means pool the profiles
taken at V0 and at V5, and V5 follows dose adjustment (by AUC at V1 in one
arm, by 5 mg/kg/day steps every 3 months up to 35 mg/kg/day in the other),
whereas the simulation doses every patient at the inclusion mean of 20.3
mg/kg; the paper does not report the V5 doses. Second, the paper's AUCinf
uses a two-point lambda_z on observed data, which is sensitive to assay noise
in the tail. The remaining Cmax shortfall is in the absorption phase and
matches the paper's own diagnostics: the phenotype-split VPC shows "the
slight underestimation of absorption predictions for rapid profiles"
(Results 3.2.2, Figure 4c), and a deviation at 10 min in the overall VPC
(Figure 4a). The parameters are used as published.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as percentages and Supplementary Table S3
  labels the same values 'IIV final model (CV%)'. They are read as the
  coefficient of variation of a log-normal parameter, so
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. If they were instead Monolix standard deviations
  (`omega = 0.6407` on ka), the variances would be 0.410 / 0.109 / 0.121 on
  ka / CL / V instead of 0.344 / 0.103 / 0.114; typical values are unaffected.
- **Residual error form.** The paper reports a combined additive (a = 1.60
  mg/L) and proportional (b = 0.35) model fitted in Monolix without naming the
  variant. Monolix's default 'combined1' form (`a + b * f` as the standard
  deviation) is used, which is `combined1()` in nlmixr2.
- **Weight covariate.** Table 2 labels beta_Cl_NBW 'Effect of body surface on
  Cl/F', but Eq. 4, the text and Supplementary Table S3 all apply it to body
  weight normalised to 34.9 kg. Body weight is used.
- **Absorption phenotype.** The covariate is observed, not estimated: a profile
  is rapid when its observed Tmax is under 1 h. It was assigned per profile in
  the study, and two patients changed from rapid to slow between visits. It is
  held constant per simulated patient here. The register name `ABS_RAPID` was
  ratified by the maintainers for this observed classification, kept separate
  from the latent mixture-class indicator `MIX_FAST_ABS`.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight is log-normal with the Table 1 mean and SD,
  truncated at 11.4 kg (lightest child) and 70 kg (an upper bound for the
  adults, whose weights are not reported). Doses are normal around 20.3
  mg/kg with SD 2.4 mg/kg, the inclusion (V0) dose; the doses at V5, after
  adjustment, are not reported. A single dose is simulated because accumulation
  over a 24-h interval is negligible (Typical-value checks).
- **Pharmacodynamics.** The haematological analysis (MCV, reticulocytes, HbF,
  neutrophils) is a set of correlations and group comparisons, not a fitted
  model, so only the PK model is packaged.
- No erratum or correction notice for the article was found as of 2026-11-21.
